The head is the word answering to the nominal core, so it stands on speech. Rule 91's rows for this shape read it that way — καταλαλιάς → evil speakings heads on speakings and δυσφημίας → evil report on report — as this chapter does at COL.2.23, ἐθελοθρησκίᾳ → will worship heading on worship, and as rule 104's εὐπειθής → easy to be entreated and εὐάρεστος → well pleasing head their stem words. Rule 66's generic-completion arm is not the case here, since speech glosses a real element rather than completing the phrase, and rule 17 forbids the competing reading's only support, that persuasiveness stands first and is the English phrase's formal head. Heading on persuasiveness remains defensible, πιθανολογία being a hapax whose distinguishing sense sits in that element.
